samples.summary: The nonce round trip is introduced as a hard backend/CLI compatibility break with no graceful degradation: a new CLI pointed at a server that does not echo `state` will 403 its own genuine redirect and hang until the 30s timeout, with no actionable error. The doc records the coupling ("a CLI at this version or later needs a backend at this version or later") but the change offers no fallback, feature negotiation, or diagnostic for self-hosted/older deployments — a notable approach-fit decision for a change whose stated issue is output formatting.

finding.evidence: rest-api.md:334-342 unchanged: "redirects to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback?code=<auth-code>`"; diff changes auth.controller.ts to append `&state=<nonce>` and github-auth.guard.ts to accept `?nonce=`.

verdict.reason: Verified directly. The backend contract did change: github-auth.guard.ts:17,39 now accepts `?mode=cli&port=<port>&nonce=<hex>` and auth.controller.ts:127-135 appends `&state=<nonce>` to the loopback redirect. But docs/design/rest-api.md:328-353, the section that explicitly presents itself as "the backend surface", still documents `GET /auth/github?mode=cli&port=<port>` and a redirect of `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback?code=<auth-code>` with no nonce and no echoed state; the risk table at :366-367 is likewise unchanged. A repo-wide case-insensitive grep for `nonce` returns only docs/design/cli.md among backend/API design docs (plus an unrelated design-editor sandbox recipe); backend.md and every other doc under docs/design/ are silent, and there is no OpenAPI/schema artifact carrying it. The one thing close to a counterexample — cli.md:168-213 documenting the full nonce round trip — does not refute the finding, because cli.md:211-213 explicitly delegates the CSRF/port-validation backend details back to rest-api.md "CLI Auth Endpoints", and rest-api.md's concrete statement of the redirect query shape is now wrong rather than merely incomplete. Under the design-doc-discipline lane (CONTRIBUTING.md:57-61: update the existing doc when evolving an area), the canonical backend-surface doc is stale and mutually contradictory with cli.md. No counterexample found.

verdict.reason: Verified independently and the presence claim holds on every point. The todo doc's Approach (docs/tasks/active/20260806-cli-status-ctx-structured-output-todo.md:19-41) scopes #635 to parseOutputFormat()/format(), status, ctx list, the schema registry, tests, and cli.md prose. Lines 116-122 add three separable changes, and all three exist in the tree: CSV formula neutralization (packages/cli/src/output/csv.ts:2-43), a cross-package OAuth nonce protocol (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:34,40,158-175,190-233 plus packages/backend/src/auth/cli-auth.store.ts:13,30,38,48,60 and the guard/controller), and a cells batch parse restructure (packages/cli/src/commands/cells.ts:117-139). The version-coupling risk the reviewer flags is documented by the repo itself at docs/design/cli.md:206-208 ("a CLI at this version or later needs a backend at this version or later") - a deployment-ordering constraint landed inside an output-formatting PR. No refutation ground applies: the code is present (not not-present), scope creep is explicitly named in this lens's lane (not out-of-scope), and CONTRIBUTING.md:67-70 only permits design+code in one PR, not bundling three unrelated subsystem changes (no counterexample). That the extra work was panel-requested does not waive it; the "Review round 2" section is the record of the expansion, not a sanction for it. Major by kind under Scope & approach fit.

verdict.reason: All claimed evidence verified. `neutralizeFormula` is applied unconditionally inside `formatCsv`'s `csvEscape` (packages/cli/src/output/csv.ts:23-26,42-52), the shared serializer. `sheets export` uses it as the machine data-export writer verbatim as quoted (packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:46, routed by detectFormat at :11-21). The reverse path does not undo it: parseCsv (packages/cli/src/util/csv-parse.ts:4-45) and buildCellMap (:82-97) pass fields through unchanged, so an exported `=SUM(B2:B10)` returns as literal `'=SUM(B2:B10)`. Cells genuinely carry formulas (packages/cli/skills/sheets-read-cells.md:44). The round trip is advertised in packages/cli/skills/recipe-csv-pipeline.md:22-45 and sheets-import-export.md:63-93 (reviewer's `skills/...` paths are repo-relative shorthand for the same files). The doc paragraph at docs/design/cli.md:854-858 scopes the behavior to `--format csv`, the global output flag handled by formatter.ts:45-68, whereas export uses the separate `--file-format` option (sheets-export.ts:29) and never calls output() — so the export-path change is undocumented. In lane as scope/approach fit: display-safety escape placed at the wrong layer (shared interchange serializer) with doc coverage narrower than actual behavior. No guard or unescaping exists to make it unreachable.

finding.summary: The nonce round trip is introduced as a hard backend/CLI compatibility break with no graceful degradation: a new CLI pointed at a server that does not echo `state` will 403 its own genuine redirect and hang until the 30s timeout, with no actionable error. The doc records the coupling ("a CLI at this version or later needs a backend at this version or later") but the change offers no fallback, feature negotiation, or diagnostic for self-hosted/older deployments — a notable approach-fit decision for a change whose stated issue is output formatting.
finding.evidence: cli.md new paragraph: "The nonce round trip is a backend contract: the loopback redirect echoes it, so a CLI at this version or later needs a backend at this version or later."; login.ts rejects a state-less code with 403 and never settles the wait.

verdict.reason: Every element of the claimed evidence verified in-tree. docs/design/cli.md:197-208 contains the quoted paragraph declaring the nonce round trip a hard backend contract ("a CLI at this version or later needs a backend at this version or later") with no negotiation or fallback. packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:227-233 rejects a callback lacking a matching `state` with 403 and explicitly does not settle the wait promise (nonceMatches returns false for a null state, line 170), so against a backend that does not echo `state` the CLI 403s its own genuine redirect and can only exit via the 30s timer at login.ts:280-288, whose message ("Login timed out. Try again with `wafflebase login`.") gives no version/compat diagnostic. The CLI always sends nonce and always requires the echo (login.ts:34-40). The echo is implemented only in this repo's backend (auth.controller.ts:127-132, cli-auth.store.ts:13-60, github-auth.guard.ts:17-39), and @wafflebase/cli is an independently published npm package (packages/cli/package.json:2-15) invoked against a user-supplied --server (login.ts:18-19), so newer-CLI/older-self-hosted-backend skew is a real deployment shape. No refutation ground holds: the code is present as described; no guard elsewhere prevents it (the backend's `state.nonce ? ...` fallback at auth.controller.ts:131 only covers the opposite direction, old CLI to new backend); and it is not out of lane, since approach/scope fit is explicitly this lens and the design doc's own risk table at docs/design/cli.md:1139 asserts the mitigation "CLI checks API compatibility on startup" for CLI/API version drift, a mitigation absent from the login path. The originating task (docs/tasks/active/20260806-cli-status-ctx-structured-output-todo.md:1,:118) is CLI output formatting with the nonce added in review round 2, which supports the finding's scope/approach-fit framing.

finding.summary: New agent-facing error codes (`INVALID_FORMAT`, `NOT_LOGGED_IN`) are not added to §10 Error Matrix, the canonical table agents/skills read for codes
finding.evidence: The change introduces two new structured error codes: `InvalidFormatError.code = 'INVALID_FORMAT'` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:15) and `NotLoggedInError.code = 'NOT_LOGGED_IN'` (packages/cli/src/commands/ctx.ts:36). §8.1 prose mentions them (docs/design/cli.md:722,725) but the canonical enumeration in §10 "Error Matrix" (lines 960-976, which lists INVALID_RANGE, FILE_EXISTS, INVALID_DOCX, etc. with exit codes) was left untouched. An agent reading the matrix to learn the code vocabulary will not find either code, nor the exit code (`ctx list` → 1) they imply.

verdict.reason: The finding claims INVALID_FORMAT and NOT_LOGGED_IN were never added to the §10 Error Matrix in docs/design/cli.md. Both are present in that exact table. The matrix heading is at docs/design/cli.md:1100 and the table runs 1102-1119; line 1104 lists "Unsupported --format value (any command) | 1 | INVALID_FORMAT | \"Invalid --format \\\"<input>\\\". Use one of: <that command's list>.\"" and line 1105 lists "`ctx list` (and other session-required commands) without a session | 1 | NOT_LOGGED_IN | \"Not logged in. Run `wafflebase login`.\"". These include the very exit code (ctx list -> 1) the reviewer said an agent could not learn from the matrix, and the messages match the source exactly (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:26,29 and packages/cli/src/commands/ctx.ts:36,39). The finding's line references are stale: it cites the matrix at 960-976 (actually 1100-1119) and §8.1 prose at 722/725 (actually 827/841/844/849), indicating it was written against an earlier revision of the doc; the reviewer's own repo-wide INVALID_FORMAT grep should have matched line 1104. The task checklist at docs/tasks/active/20260806-cli-status-ctx-structured-output-todo.md:111 also records this item as completed, consistent with the working tree.

finding.summary: §8.1 now promises `INVALID_FORMAT` for any unsupported `--format`, but the content/export commands it explicitly names still emit code `ERROR`
finding.evidence: The added prose reads: "An unsupported `--format` value is rejected with `"code": "INVALID_FORMAT"` rather than ignored. Validation is per-command because `docs`/`slides`/`notes` `content` and `export` deliberately reuse the same global `--format` flag …". That sentence tells an agent those commands also report INVALID_FORMAT, but `parseContentFormat` (packages/cli/src/docs/content.ts:27) throws a plain `Error`, so `outputError`'s `errorCode()` falls back to `'ERROR'` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:75). The same holds for `detectExportFormat` in packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:39 and the slides/notes equivalents. Either those validators should carry `code = 'INVALID_FORMAT'` or the doc should scope the claim to `output()` commands only.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `parseContentFormat` (packages/cli/src/docs/content.ts:27) throws a plain `Error` so `errorCode()` falls back to `'ERROR'`, contradicting the §8.1 prose. That code is not present as described. `parseContentFormat` throws `new InvalidFormatError(value, VALID_CONTENT_FORMATS)` (docs/content.ts:26-31), and `InvalidFormatError` carries `readonly code = 'INVALID_FORMAT'` (output/formatter.ts:25-31), which `errorCode()` preserves (formatter.ts:88-94) and `outputError` emits (formatter.ts:104-110); `docs content` routes its throw through `outputError` (commands/docs.ts:220-222). `detectExportFormat` likewise throws `InvalidFormatError(formatFlag, VALID_EXPORT_FORMATS)` for a bad `--format` (commands/docs.ts:40-46); its plain `Error` at docs.ts:50-52 is only the cannot-infer-from-extension case, which the doc explicitly scopes out ("A format that cannot be *inferred* ... stays a plain `ERROR`", cli.md:850-852). The slides/notes equivalents behave identically (slides/content.ts:24-29, notes/content.ts:10, commands/slides.ts:203, commands/notes.ts:196). The doc sentence is therefore accurate and the alleged doc/code divergence does not exist.
